claims: After five minutes without a request, the preview says "unavailable" even when data exists. `trove-og-data.ts:274` — `unstable_cache` has `revalidate: 60` while the age check allows 5 minutes; an entry older than 5 minutes becomes `null` and nothing waits for the refresh (never calls `fetchTroveOgDataForCache` outside the cache), so shares get "indexed snapshot unavailable" and the wrong image may stay cached via `s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`
`null` results ("not found", bad data, a trove not indexed yet) are cached with no `fetchedAtMs` (`:203`, `:212-214`), so they are never age-checked; a stale `null` would still be served
Tests don't cover it: the test file replaces `unstable_cache` with a pass-through (`trove-og-data.test.ts:12-25`), and the test at `:227` only checks the freshness predicate

Background refresh failures write whole error bodies to server logs. `trove-og-data.ts:247`, with the error class at `lib/graphql-fetch.ts:24-36` — `ClientError` exposes `response` (full upstream `body`) and `request`, and `fetchTroveOgDataForCache` lets that error escape inside `unstable_cache`

The browser test fixture doesn't handle the two new queries: `tests/browser/fixtures/hasura-fixture-server.mjs:1888` has no case for `CdpTroveOgCollaterals` or `CdpTroveOgById`, so every trove-page browser run quietly shows the "unavailable" preview and the data-backed card is never exercised
`trove-og-data.ts:184`: the "Exported for tests" comment sits on a function that isn't exported
`fetchTroveOgDataUncached` exists only for tests and wraps a `catch` that production code never runs
`shortTroveId` is copied into `page.tsx:48` when it could be imported from `_og/trove-og-card.tsx:115`
11-character values like `28.08K GBPm` at about 137px in a 126px-wide tile, so the text may spill over

judge_reasoning.3882085361: The review notes that resolveMetadataBase trusts x-forwarded-host, but it explicitly clears this ('isn't a cache-poisoning risk'). It never identifies the missing host allowlist as a defect.
judge_reasoning.3882086206: The review flags duplication of shortTroveId in page.tsx, not the icrTone/icrTextClass threshold duplication.
judge_reasoning.3882090788: The review does not mention IPv6 loopback ([::1]) handling in site-metadata.ts.
judge_reasoning.3882119274: The review never raises event-time ICR being shown as a fresh health signal. It says the card's ICR logic matches the header.
judge_reasoning.3882119284: The review mentions the s-maxage=60/stale-while-revalidate=300 headers, but only as a way an 'unavailable' image persists. It does not raise the compounding of the 5-minute data age with the image cache age, which leaves data about 11 minutes stale.

1.why: trove-og-data.ts:22/263 sets unstable_cache revalidate to 60s, and :274 turns data older than TROVE_OG_MAX_DATA_AGE_MS (5 min) into null. unstable_cache serves the stale entry and refreshes in the background (the repo says so at server-cache.ts:287 and pool-detail-ssr.ts:291), so the first request after 5+ idle minutes renders 'unavailable' when data exists. The known :54 item is about combined cache age, which is a different issue.

2.why: It's true that null results carry no fetchedAtMs (:203, :212-214). But a stale data entry older than 5 min is already mapped to null at :274, so serving a stale cached null gives the same result the age check would. No separate defect.

3.why: trove-og-data.test.ts:12-25 replaces unstable_cache with a pass-through that returns fn. The test at :227 only calls troveOgDataIsFresh, so nothing tests the stale-cache interaction in claim 1.

4.why: ClientError (graphql-fetch.ts:24-36) does expose response.body and request, and errors do escape unstable_cache. But the body is a Hasura error body with no secret (og-graphql-client sends no admin header), so no concrete harm is named.

5.why: The fixture switch has cases for HomepageOgDailySnapshots and PoolOgDailySnapshots but none for CdpTroveOgCollaterals or CdpTroveOgById, so those fall to unhandledOperation (a GraphQL error). trove-history.test.ts:48 visits the trove page, so every run gets the null, 'unavailable' card.

6.why: trove-og-data.ts:184 says '@internal Exported for focused data-contract tests' above `async function fetchTroveOgData`, which is not exported. The exported wrapper is at :218.

7.why: Correct that fetchTroveOgDataUncached is only imported by the test file. But that follows an existing repo pattern (peg-og-data.ts fetchPegMonitoringOgDataUncached, '@internal Exported for testing'), so it's a design preference, not a defect.

8.why: The diff adds `shortTroveId` at page.tsx:48, identical to the exported `shortTroveId` at _og/trove-og-card.tsx:115, which opengraph-image.tsx already imports. Duplication of the same kind as the known icrTone item.

9.why: The tile content width works out to 126px: 1200 minus 96 padding minus 360 left column gives 744; minus 52 panel padding and border gives 692; minus 36 of gaps, divided by 4 tiles gives 164; minus 38 tile padding and border gives 126. STAT_VALUE_STYLE is nowrap, 22px, weight 700, letterSpacing -0.5. Measuring with the bundled Geist 700 woff advance widths gives '28.08K GBPm' ≈ 146px and '44.79K USDm' ≈ 144px, so the text spills over.
